topics.topic: Publication mark timestamp authority, instant, read timing/count, representation, and precision
questions: What authoritative time source supplies the fresh `marked_at` instant when a mark is created?
In what representation is `marked_at` stored: offset-aware UTC, UTC without an offset, local time, or another form?
How many readings of the time source does one mark operation take, and at what point relative to taking the project lock and writing the record?
Which authority supplies `marked_at`, when is it read during a mark operation, how many readings occur, and is the stored datetime offset-aware UTC or UTC without an offset?
What instant does a fresh publication mark record, where does that instant come from, what datetime representation and precision are stored, and how many readings does one mark operation take?

quotes:
The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.
judgement.why: This is the same timestamp-authority, sampling, representation and precision question already decided by P1, and the quoted A7 passages have not changed.

precedent.why: A7 identifies the clock authority, fixes the single sampling point and read count, and specifies the exact UTC-naive microsecond representation and serialization.

topics.topic: Scope of the replay exception permitting creation of the project lock and its folders, and its reconciliation with guarantees, models, and tests
questions: Does “the folders leading to it” mean only folders below an already existing configured state folder, or does it include the configured state folder that A6 rule 2 says the service never creates?
Must INV-06 be qualified to allow creation of the absent project lock and its permitted folders, as A3 rule 2 now does?
What must the INV-06 test show about an initially absent project lock, its folders, marks, temporary files, and all other durable state now that replay has a stated lock-scaffolding exception?
Is the State 0 guarantee revised so that a repeated delivery may create the project lock and its required folders?
Does “changes nothing” exclude the newly permitted creation of a project lock and its folders, or must P-06 be amended?
Must M04's meaning permit the project-lock and folder creation introduced by A3 rule 2?
Does INV-06 exclude creation of the project lock file and its leading folders, or must a repeated placement truly make no durable filesystem change?

What must the INV-06 test show when the placement exists but the project lock file or its leading folders are absent: that they are created as the declared exception, or that no filesystem entry at all is added?
Must INV-06, P-06, R0-15 and M04 permit creation of an absent project lock file and its folders during a repeated placement, or must a replay leave all durable state unchanged?

quotes:
An absent project lock file and the folders leading to it
   are the one exception: taking the lock creates them (A6 rules 2 and 4).
- INV-06: at most one placement exists per project and source content, and a repeated placement writes nothing.
judgement.divergence: One implementation creates the absent lock file and permitted folders during replay; another permits no replay write and therefore must avoid creation or refuse, which the caller and filesystem operator notice.
judgement.why: A3 expressly permits replay to create lock scaffolding while INV-06 unqualifiedly says a repeated placement writes nothing.

topics.topic: Required concurrency, calls, and ordering for INV-12 test witnesses
questions: Must the mark calls overlap and race for the lock, or is it sufficient to issue them sequentially merely from one or more processes?
Which calls and ordering must produce these three outcomes when only two distinct `photo_id` values are named?
What exact calls and ordering must each INV-12 witness perform so that both replay of the winning photo_id and conflict for the other photo_id are required?

quotes: - INV-12: concurrent calls for one project never produce two placements or two marks for one source.

- INV-12: concurrent placements of one source, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed` and leave one placement record and one stored image (`test_separate_processes_leave_one_placement`), and marks of two `photo_id` values, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other, and leave one mark record holding the `photo_id` whose call answered `marked` (`test_concurrent_calls_leave_one_placement_and_one_mark`, `test_separate_processes_leave_one_mark`).

The same `photo_id` again answers `replayed` with the first mark. Another `photo_id` is refused
   with `publication_conflict` and nothing changes.
judgement.why: INV-12 requires genuinely concurrent calls, its Required tests item requires both in-process and separate-process witnesses and all three mark outcomes, and A4 fixes replay for the winning photo_id and conflict for the other.

topics.topic: Behavior of a process that loses a race to create an absent project lock
questions: When two processes both observe an absent lock and one exclusive creation succeeds while the other receives an already-exists result, must the loser reopen the new file as an existing lock and wait, or treat its creation failure as a refusal?

quotes:
The service makes the folders below the binary store and the state folder exist one at a time, from
   the outermost: a folder it finds is accepted, whoever created it, also a concurrent call, when it is a
   folder, and a creation that finds the folder already there is not a failure; a missing one is created with the mode of the imported `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the
   binary store and of the imported `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the state folder, set whatever the
   process umask.

When it already exists it is opened
   for reading and writing without following a link and used as it stands: its mode and its bytes are
   never changed or read, so taking the lock writes nothing.
A wait ends only when the lock is taken or the process ends.
judgement.why: An already-existing result is handled by the existing-lock rule: the loser opens the file without following links and waits until it takes the operating-system lock.

topics.topic: Behavior when a valid mark record has no corresponding placement record
questions: What must scan, delivery, and mark do when a valid mark record exists but the corresponding placement record is absent?

quotes:
`capability:delivery_store.read_placement` and `capability:delivery_store.read_mark` read both records, so a
   damaged record stops the delivery. With an existing placement the flow answers `replayed`, with the `photo_id` of
   its mark if there is one.
`capability:source_folder.read_named_source` applies condition 1 of A3 rule 5 and reads the file once.
`capability:delivery_store.write_placement` writes the record, and the lock is released.
judgement.why: The later delivery flow reads both records, stops only for a damaged record, replays only when a placement exists, and otherwise continues through source reading and placement writing; a schema-valid orphan mark is therefore retained while the missing placement is created.

topics.topic: Delivery behavior when a valid placement has a damaged mark record
questions: When a valid placement exists but its mark record is damaged, must delivery return `replayed` without a `photo_id`, or refuse the whole operation with STATE_UNAVAILABLE?

quotes:
Delivering content that already has a placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the
   current `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, whatever name the request carries and even
   when the source file has left the folder.

A record that is a link, even a dangling one, or that
   cannot be opened or read, is not valid JSON, fails that validation or names another project or source
   is never taken for an absent record: the operation is refused with the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode, whose value is
   `state_unavailable`, and changes no record and no stored image.
judgement.divergence: One passage requires a successful replay of the existing placement, while the other requires a STATE_UNAVAILABLE refusal because the damaged mark record is not treated as absent; the delivery caller sees the difference.
judgement.why: A3's unconditional existing-placement replay and A6's operation-wide damaged-record refusal give different outcomes for a placement whose corresponding mark record is damaged.

quotes:
In the state
   folder an entry on the way that is a symbolic link or not a folder fails the write, and a failure to
   create a folder or set its mode fails it too; for the lock file that is the refusal of rule 5.

A record is absent only when no entry exists at its address, also when a folder on its address does
   not exist; reading a record creates nothing. A placement or mark record is opened
   without following a link and validated as JSON against its closed model: every field present with its
   type, every enumeration value a member, every nested model valid, and no other field.
judgement.divergence: One implementation follows a symbolic-link ancestor below the state folder and accepts the target record; another applies no-follow semantics to every component and refuses with STATE_UNAVAILABLE.
